chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabīʿ from Abu ʿAbdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever entrusts a drinker of wine with a trust, after knowing his condition, has no guarantee from Allah (Exalted and Mighty), nor does he have a reward, nor a substitute.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence of entrusting a known drinker of wine with a trust?
ai.summary: In the context of *al-Ijarat* (contracts/trusts) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that while a *sharib al-khamr* (drinker of wine) is generally considered trustworthy (*thiqah*) for financial matters, deliberate entrustment after full knowledge of his vice results in the loss of divine guarantee (*daman*) and reward (*ajr*). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between legal capacity for transactions and spiritual merit, emphasizing that the entrusting party bears the risk of the trustee's moral failing when the choice is informed.
